claim_checks.claim: Lice-attributed share of total sea-sojourn mortality: long-distance smolts 25.3% vs inner-fjord smolts 14.7%; veteran migrants 14.8% vs 1.7% inner-fjord
claim_checks.extract_quote: The fraction of total mortality attributed to lice during sea-sojourn was greater for long-distance migrants (smolts: 25.3%; veteran migrants: 14.8%) versus those remaining within the inner-fjord (smolts: 14.7%; veteran migrants: 1.7%).

claim_checks.claim: Population-level lice-attributed mortality ranged 3.3%–34.3% across five Sognefjorden rivers despite shared lice field — driven by individual migration distance
claim_checks.extract_quote: This resulted in an unequal contribution of lice to total mortality among populations (range: 3.3%–34.3%).

claim_checks.claim: N = 8,049 simulated trajectories (4,234 smolts, 3,815 veterans) from acoustic telemetry of N = 517 fish (175 smolts, 342 veterans); 2013–2015
claim_checks.extract_quote: We utilized simulated individual migration trajectories of facultatively anadromous brown trout (Salmo trutta) (N = 8049), generated from spatialtemporal fjord-use models fitted to empirical tracking data (N = 517).

claim_checks.claim: Outer-fjord lice densities highest near farms (>67,000 t salmon biomass ~3.6M fish in 2015); inner fjord protected since National Salmon Fjord designation 2007
claim_checks.extract_quote: Highest densities were modeled in the outer-fjord at a closer vicinity to aquaculture facilities... the inner fjord region has never been widely used for aquaculture, and formal protection against aquaculture development was granted in 2007.

claim_checks.claim: Minimum migration to mid-fjord: 8.5–48.8 km by population; mid fjord 75.2 km / 376 km², outer 93.3 km / 1,041 km² — most trout now remain ≤ mid-fjord vs >200 km historically
claim_checks.note: Specific distances and areas are not mentioned in the extract.

claim_checks.claim: Individual migration trajectory selection — not population-level average exposure — is the primary driver of differential lice-induced mortality
claim_checks.extract_quote: Despite an equal distribution of lice exposure for all populations within the fjord, diverse mortality consequences among populations were estimated, largely resulting from individual selection of migration trajectory.

claim_checks.claim: Most brown trout remained in the inner fjord (protected from aquaculture), keeping population-average infestation below critical mortality thresholds
claim_checks.extract_quote: As most brown trout remained in the inner-fjord, an area protected from aquaculture, individual accumulated levels of lice exposure and infestation were low, resulting in infestation estimates largely below critical-mortality thresholds.

claim_checks.claim: Lice densities were highest in the outer fjord near aquaculture facilities; limited year-to-year variation was observed 2013-2015
claim_checks.extract_quote: A gradient of lice was spatially distributed throughout the fjord. Highest densities were modeled in the outer-fjord at a closer vicinity to aquaculture facilities. Accordingly, estimates of accumulated lice infestation were higher for individuals that underwent long-distance migrations, residing for longer in the outer-fjord, with limited differences observed between years.

claim_checks.claim: The seaward extent of Sognefjorden sea trout migration has declined over 60 years, coinciding with aquaculture expansion
claim_checks.extract_quote: The seaward extent of migration in Sognefjorden has diminished over a 60-year period and since the introduction of aquaculture in the region.

evidence_direction_note: The evidence direction 'supports_effect' is consistent with the extract, which indicates that lice exposure affects mortality.
